messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@polaris.com>

Subject: Major latency spike / 500s hitting checkout (urgent)

Logan,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and increased 5xx errors from Redwood for our checkout service since ~07:45 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6.5% and median tail latency is 4.2s for text-generation calls. This is affecting live traffic — customers are abandoning carts.

Attached: polaris-service-metrics-20261115.csv (10MB) — contains request/latency/error buckets.

We have an active incident on our side (PD: POL-9218). Please confirm immediate next steps and ETA for mitigation. Our CTO (Tim) is on standby.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Ops Lead, Polaris Commerce

Date: 2026-11-15T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Major latency spike / 500s hitting checkout (urgent)

Seeing the traces now. Initial notes:
- Kernel-side GPU queue depth spiked; observed increased token-latency variance starting 07:40 PT.
- KV cache churn from competing models (two simultaneous heavy prefixes) increased memory pressure and caused more CPU fallbacks on smaller infra nodes.
- A temporary mis-scheduling of lower-priority batches onto the Polaris pool looks likely; investigating scheduler logs (pdq-scheduler).

Actions I'm taking (ETA in parentheses):
1) Pull affected pool and move Polaris traffic to isolation fallback pool (manual re-route) — 15 min.
2) Enable conservative batching profile for Polaris (reduce batch size, increase dedicate threads) — 20 min.
3) Capture full kernel traces and export (attaching) for postmortem — ongoing.

Attachment: kernel-trace-20261115.zip (14MB) — contains a short set of stack traces and scheduler samples.

If re-route is successful we'll expect initial visible improvement in error rate within 10–15 minutes, tail latency improvement in ~30.

Vivek
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime

Polaris Ops team,

We’re aware of elevated error rates and increased latency affecting checkout requests. Our engineers are actively rerouting traffic to an isolated pool and applying conservative batching to reduce tail latency. We expect measurable improvement within 30 minutes. We will send another update at 09:00 PT or earlier if there is a material change.

Best,
Marissa (on behalf of Redwood Incident Response)

C-suite snapshot (one paragraph) draft:
Redwood observed an anomalous scheduler/KV cache interaction impacting a dedicated Polaris serving pool that increased per-request tail latency and 5xx rates starting ~07:40 PT. We are re-routing traffic to an isolated fallback pool and applying a reduced-batch execution profile. Expected remediation is partial within 30 minutes with full stabilization in under 2 hours. Financial exposure: ongoing, early estimate is <24 hrs of degraded checkout throughput; we will quantify once stable.

Please review and sign off; I can send to Polaris ops if you OK.

Attachment: cs_status_draft_1115.pdf (1 page)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: C-suite snapshot: Polaris outage (09:05 PT)

Executive Snapshot — Polaris Commerce incident (09:05 PT)
- Impact: ~12% of checkout requests routed to affected variant experienced >1s tail increase; 5xx rate peaked at 6.5% (customer reported). Live revenue impact observed — customer reports cart abandonment.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): scheduler-induced KV-cache churn when two heavy prefixes share pool; fallback CPU execution on lower-tier nodes.
- Immediate mitigations: 1) Manual reroute to isolated fallback pool (in progress), 2) conservative batching profile, 3) pause low-priority batch jobs on same cluster.
- ETA: visible error-rate reduction within 15 min; tail-latency improvement within 30–45 min; full stabilization in ~90–120 min.
- Customer comms: short status + ETA at 09:00 PT, followed by post-incident RCA.
- Exec ask: Acknowledge potential crediting/discount conversation if full recovery takes >12 hours and revenue loss confirmed.

I'll prepare a one-slide summary for the exec call.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
